Favorite variants:

Heroic Infinitor- This variant turns a villain I dread playing into one of my absolute favorite fights. posts.name: FrivYeti
posts.cooked:
So now I'm thinking about having those Dark Watch variants listed above. 

Setback: Second Chances

Power: Consider. Discard a card. If you do, draw two cards. Add or remove an unlucky token from Setback.

We've got one Setback who does the random plays to boost his pool, and one who reduces his pool to protect people, so it seems like the third variation is one who has better control over his hand and luck pool. Not total control, because he's still Setback, but more tactical.

Mr. Fixer: Black Fist

Power: Kung-Fu. Discard up to three cards. Mr. Fixer deals X Melee damage to a target, where X is the number of cards discarded.

Mr. Fixer is limited by needing to do damage, and us not really wanting a power that's just "base, but better". This one replaces the "blow things up" damage power with a "focus your energies" power that conveniently gives you a use for all those Styles and Tools you aren't playing. 

Expatriette: Reluctant Student

Power: Overwatch. Until the start of your next turn, the first time a Hero target takes damage each turn, Expatriette may deal the source of that damage 1 Projectile damage. 

It's a version of Expatriette who's watching and learning from people, instead of charging in, and also kind of a neat power. 

Nightmist: Gateway To Beyond

Power: Be The Gate. Another player may play a card. Nightmist deals herself 2 Infernal damage. 

I may have lost good ideas by the time I reached Nightmist.

And I've had a new idea for Nightmist, although it's a little complicated.

Power: Gateway To Beyond. Nightmist deals herself up to 3 Infernal damage. Put a hero variant card into play in any player's play area with HP equal to twice the damage Nightmist took. It cannot heal. If destroyed, remove it from the game.

posts.name: Yoshi348
posts.cooked:
Mostly focusing on things that haven't been said already, or that have been said and I disagree with:

  • I'm honestly not much of a fan of Termination AZ. It's not that the ability can't be potent - I have seen it do some ludicrous things - but that it really feels like a "win-more" power. If AZ gets setup and stable he's generally doing very very well for himself anyway, and it's not often that you really need the stupidity that Violent Shivers provides. On the other side, if AZ is struggling you essentially have no power and no way to get going. I mean, the same thing applies a little bit to his base power but you generally only need one piece of equipment to get some value out of that, whereas Violent Shivers is a lot more risky with just one card, especially depending on the villian.
  • I'm really going to have to speak up for Bunker and be pretty suprised about some of the comments on TN Bunker. I've always found that TN Bunker has the problem where the play a card part isn't that potent because you just nuked one of your old card plays, and the power part isn't helpful on its own because you just used a power, so when you use this, it's usually a way to get rid of a bad card for a hopefully good one and maybe play it and power it immediately, making it a more unreliable version of the base power with a bit of potential upside. I find usually once Turret Mode gets into play I want it to stay there, while the other two you can't power out of. I feel like it only really gets good use when Bunker gets free random card plays of the top of his deck, like with Mission Control or Santa Guise or something. Also, shoutouts to F6 Bunker for being the most reliable Ongoing destroyer in the game from a starting hand; Visionary and Parse have more sustained destruction, but Bunker's the most likely to shut things down out of the gate with 9 cards to be used for it. It's pretty fitting that it's great against Iron Legacy.
  • I want to stick up for Dark Watch Mr. Fixer and even call it the most well designed variant card in the entire game. It's a truly transformative card that makes him play completely differently. The key is to just consider your items one shots that deal big damage, and even without donated card plays or fodder cards from other players I feel like you still contribute very well with a unique strength and weakness profile compared to standard Mr. Fixer.
  • Though it's been covered, I'd like to point out that the only reason Hunted Naturalist doesn't completely obsolesce regular Naturalist is that he can't fish up 1 DR from the rhino card at will, making regular Naturalist a much better tank, especially since the other rhino tank cards feed off that baseline DR. The same doesn't apply for his other forms, since playing two cards a turn more than makes up for the lack of +1 attack and gazelle doesn't even have a passive at all.
  • Horus Ra and Eternal Haka both have the problem that they let you dig for cards but because they replace a base damage card they cause you to HAVE to dig for cards that you wouldn't have had to dig for in the first place. Both decks also have a pretty even card quality and utility so you wouldn't be digging for cards in the first place in most matches; it's really only for specific fights where you really want Flesh of the Sun God or Savage Mana.
  • Adamant Dr. Medico's Regeneration is a poor replacement for regular Mainstay's Block. If you use the variant teams as an unseperatable whole, I'd definitely consider the Adamant team a downgrade on that reason alone, because Block is your only defense against light to moderate AoE eating you alive and ruining your whack-a-mole approach to surviving.
  • The worst part about Team Leader Tachyon is that you yourself become very weak outside of your power, with Tachyon herself really suffering from the lack of a constant outlet to fill your trash. You basically give up on doing anything useful on your own just to boringly but powerfully stuff cards in other people's hands. It's not like true support characters where you're making a lot of decisions on what kind of support the team needs when, either, you mostly just play a weak card or two, use power, and then pass.

Whatever sounds best, I think.  Team Leader Tachyon is catchier than F6 Tachyon.  Also, for most of them, it wasn't always obvious what their official name should be, I think.  

Variants I see named after their powers:

Team Leader Tachyon
AZ Elemental Wrath
Requital Captain Cosmic
Redeemer Fanatic
Bitter Fixer
 

Of these, DW Mr. Fixer is the only one that has a subtitle on their card.

posts.name: bobbertoriley
posts.cooked:
I still think the best name for Fused/Requital is Super Cosmic Bros., but it never caught on. :(

 

I always wished that cards like Fused Cosmic and Redeemer Fanatic had been given subtitles in the same way we have Parse: Fugue State or Rook City Wraith, at least printed on the card.

posts.name: darkroydante
posts.cooked: Yeah, Requital doesn’t have a subtitle (subname?) I know Fused was a popular name for him. In the video game, his name is Captain Cosmic Requital, so that’s probably as official as it’s going to get.
